title: Ringdown queue - garland handoff (midwatch)
body:
Summary:

Quick midwatch handoff capturing ongoing elevated user-facing tail latency on text-generation endpoints (hosted-api). Root cause suspected: unbounded growth in in-memory KV cache on a subset of serving pods after a soft-failure in the prefix-eviction path. Impact intermittent but reproducible under sustained multi-tenant burst (region: us-west2).

High-level timeline (local times):
- 00:10: first pager: p95/p99 drift observed for model rdx-gpt-medium on route /v1/generate (latency spike to 1.2s from baseline 220ms).
- 00:16: automated autoscaler triggered burst scale but latency remained high on new pods (suggests per-pod issue).
- 00:22: SRE oncall did quick pod-heap-check; noticed high RSS and KV-cache size on 3/12 pods.
- 00:30: temporary mitigation: applied config to lower per-request KV retention window to 30s (was 5m) via feature-flag. Partial improvement for new requests.
- 00:48: deep-dive showed a bug in the cache-eviction comparator that fails to evict certain prefixes that contain long-lived external-tool tokens, causing retention blowup.
- 01:05: Cache reaper cron scheduled as hotfix across affected nodes; downstream verification looked better.
- 01:40: handoff to midwatch: system recovering but still frag: background reaper is running and some pods still show elevated memory. Follow-ups required for a durable fix.

Current status at handoff:
- User traffic: mostly restored. p95 ~ 270ms, p99 ~ 420ms (still slightly above baseline). Error rates stable.
- Affected pods: 3 pods (node-117, node-118, node-119) flagged for manual inspection.
- Temporary mitigations applied: KV retention window lowered via feature toggle; reaper cron patched and deployed to canary then rolled to cluster.
- Pager escalation closed at 00:58 after reaper verified.

Immediate actions for next shift (owner -> Aisha -> oncall-midwatch / assignee on rotation):
1) Keep the reaper running for at least 6 hours with increased logging (reaper.log level=DEBUG). Watch for steady decrease in per-pod KV size. If any pod does not reduce memory within 90 minutes, collect heap profile and escalate to infra-oncall.
2) Rollout plan for full fix: revert temp retention window change only after feature-branch landed (PR referenced below) and validated on canary. Do not revert earlier than 24h post-fix.
3) Add a transient alert: kv-cache-growth-rate > 30MB/min for > 3 consecutive minutes for more than 2 pods -> Pager (P1). Currently only logged.
4) For any pod with RSS > 14GB repeatedly, perform a graceful restart and attach heap profile to JIRA ticket.

Runbook diffs / draft edits (need review and merge):
- Name: serving-runtime/kv-cache-runbook (draft)
- Suggested new steps (prepend under "Emergency mitigation"):
  * Step 1: enable-feature-flag: kv.retention_window=30s (apply to routing config service). Command: curl -XPOST $CONTROLPLANE/api/flags -d '{"kv.retention_window":30}'
  * Step 2: trigger reaper job immediately: kubectl -n serving apply -f reaper-hotfix.yaml
  * Step 3: if growth persists, scale down signal-processing threads to 2 for target pods: kubectl set env deployment/serving-pool SIGNAL_THREADS=2
- Add a note: "Do not disable cache entirely; prefer retention window adjustments or reaper. Disabling cache has >2x cost impact."

Investigation notes (tech detail):
- Heap profiles collected from node-118 at 00:40 show bucketed prefix maps with degenerate comparator ordering; most buckets referenced by a small subset of tenants but never marked eligible for eviction. Reproduction steps in staging attached in PR.
- Hypothesis: comparator uses ephemeral Last-Access timestamp that, under a race with background refill, gets updated preventing eviction. Looks like a classic read-after-write ordering bug introduced in commit a1b2c3 (model-serving: prefix-eviction: use monotonic clock).

Commands / checkpoints used during mitigation (for audit):
- kubectl logs -n serving deployment/serving-pool -c runtime --since=2h | grep KVCache
- curl -sS $CONTROLPLANE/api/flags | jq '.kv'
- kubectl apply -f infra/hotfixes/reaper-hotfix.yaml
- gcloud compute ssh node-118 -- "sudo pmap -x $(pgrep serving-runtime) | head -n 40"

Open follow-ups (owners and target dates):
- SRE / Infra: create stable reaper operator that is workload-aware (owner: Diego Martins) - target: 2026-09-10
- Serving Runtime team: patch comparator bug + unit tests (owner: Maya Chen) - PR ready: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR/452 - target: 2026-09-06
- Product / Release: add a canary gate for retention-window feature flag changes (owner: Rory Patel) - target: 2026-09-08
- Observability: add kv-cache-growth-rate metric to main dashboards + alerting rule (owner: Aisha Raman) - target: 2026-09-05

Notes to next oncall:
- Check dashboards: "Serving -> Model latency -> rdx-gpt-medium" and "Infra -> Memory by pod -> serving-pool". If trend reappears, do not immediately scale cluster bigger without checking per-pod memory. Scaling hides per-pod memory leaks and increases blast-radius.
- If reaper job seems stuck (no logs for >10m), run the sanity probe: kubectl exec -it pod/<pod> -n serving -- /bin/reaperctl status
- Heap profiles are stored in s3://redwood-heap-profiles/2026-09-03/; tag any collected sample with pod & timestamp in JIRA ticket SRE-2143.

Unresolved questions (for postmortem):
- Why did autoscaler not mitigate impact for new pods? (possible shared init path or cold-start warmup missing KV cap)
- Is the comparator bug single-tenant triggered (i.e., by long-lived external-tool tokens) or systemic? Need tenant correlation.
- Should we expose a per-tenant soft-eviction knob to limit attack surface?

Suggested postmortem outline (skeleton):
1) Summary and impact window
2) Timeline and detection path
3) Root cause analysis (bug + workload condition)
4) Short-term mitigation steps done during incident
5) Long-term fixes (reaper operator + comparator patch + monitoring)
6) Action item tracker with owners and dates
7) Lessons learned: e.g., "do not rely solely on autoscaler for memory-related issues"

Attachments / artifacts to review in postmortem:
- PR 452 (fix + test vectors)
- Heap profile snapshots (s3 links in ticket)
- Alert history and runbook edits diff (Confluence draft)

Hand-off quick checklist (tick off during takeover):
- [ ] Verify reaper logs showing progress in last 20m
- [ ] Confirm no new p99 spike in last 15m
- [ ] Ensure hotfix flag still enabled and not auto-reverted by rollout
- [ ] Pick up outstanding follow-ups in JIRA SRE-2143

If anything regresses or you need immediate help, escalate to oncall-senior and ping #sre-ops with subject "kv-cache-growth P1".

End of midwatch handoff.

-- Aisha (oncall)
